scope: Read-only source review; no compilation/native run and no edits to combined checkout. Qualification still requires original native CI and repository gates.

finding_closed.original: message_request_id matches server Request as well as Response/Error, but server/client counters independently start at zero. Request{id:n} before Response{id:n} would be consumed and cause bail rather than remain pending.
finding_closed.counterexample: With current client id n and pending [server Request{id:n}, client Response{id:n}], old predicate selected the Request. Corrected predicate selects only the Response and retains the Request.
finding_closed.correction: New helper predicate explicitly matches Response/Error ids; Request/Notification return false. Existing ordinary read/request methods remain unchanged.

reviewed_boundaries: Fresh client id allocated by unchanged send_request on every attempt.
Only exact -32603, data None, and the two full pre-admission refusal strings can retry; no fuzzy text or general internal-error retry.
send serialization/write/flush failure, read/parse failure, disconnect, timeout, response decoding failure and other errors terminate without resubmission.
One outer tokio timeout encloses all sends, response reads, parsing and 25 ms backoffs; timeout budget is not reset per attempt.
Nonmatching responses/errors and server requests/notifications remain in the existing pending buffer.
Production turn_processor maps NotSubmitted to the exact NotIdle error; terminalizing error originates before io.submit_turn_input or pending admission registration.
New callsites are successful fixture setup/next-turn paths; thread_resume rejection requests and their negative assertions remain ordinary and intact.
Explicit suite durations remain as passed; default helper uses existing DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT (Windows 25 s, other platforms 10 s). No timeout increase added.
limits: The shared start_turn_and_wait_for_completion now bounds turn admission by existing default request timeout; previously it relied on its caller timeout. Completion wait and matching thread/turn check remain unchanged.
Source review is not native or Windows execution evidence.
